gen-gf-calligraffitti-gf-lexend-peta: Lexend Peta reads wide and friendly, its curves staying full where other letters would thin out. But Calligraffitti sits on top like marker scrawl, and a long run of the plain sans would feel steady beneath it.
gen-gf-calligraffitti-gf-lexend-tera: Calligraffitti looks traced in marker, with a towering midzone and counters spilling outward. Its scrawl carries the personality, while Lexend Tera, a plain sans drawn like plotter-pen line, handles the quiet, spaced-out work of being read.
gen-gf-calligraffitti-gf-lexend-zetta: Friendly, first of all: Calligraffitti leans in with marker-traced strokes. Lexend Zetta stands tall and widely tracked beneath it, so the handwriting feels warm and loose while the sans feels measured and modern.
gen-gf-cambo-gf-cascadia-code: Cascadia Code reads like wire, with a smooth path around every bend and neighbors held well apart. Its sans-serif monoline neon-tube thickness against Cambo's gently pressured brush strokes is the sharpest thing about this pairing.
gen-gf-cambo-gf-cascadia-mono: Cambo's small letters are thick with height, like bundled cable. Cascadia Mono, a plain sans with a marker-nib line that ignores direction, stands against those softly modulated serif strokes like pins in a wide board.
gen-gf-cambo-gf-julius-sans-one: Julius Sans One reads open and spacious, with capitals and lowercase nearly level and curves left unclosed. Cambo, meanwhile, adds gentle weight change where its bowls curve, so the serif feels traditional beside the plain sans.
gen-gf-cambo-gf-lexend-exa: Cambo leads with editorial, traditional serif letters whose brush-like strokes carry a slight but visible thick-thin variation. Lexend Exa answers in a sans-serif with one level beat, wide curves, and stubby ascenders beside a big x-height.
gen-gf-cambo-gf-lexend-giga: Restrained serif meets flat linework. Lexend Giga, a plain sans with generous tracking and no pinched joins, would let a long page move along while Cambo keeps its modest gap between thick and thin.
gen-gf-cambo-gf-lexend-mega: Cambo brings a modest weight shift inside each stroke, traditional and editorial in tone. Lexend Mega, a plain sans with a pipe-cleaner feel and a visible gap in every c, would read lightly and openly across a long page.
gen-gf-cambo-gf-lexend-peta: Lexend Peta is wide-mouthed and full, with no thinning in its curves. Cambo's moderate contrast sits above it, neither stark nor flat, so the serif brings a traditional editorial voice and the plain sans keeps things approachable.
